## Install — no GitHub CLI, no tokens, no SSH keys

Download the **Source code (zip)** below, extract, and run the bundled installer. Same flow on every OS.

**macOS / Linux**
```bash
cd jtr-0.7.0
./install.sh
```

**Windows**
```powershell
cd .\jtr-0.7.0\
powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File .\install.ps1
```

The installer fetches `uv` if needed, then runs `uv tool install` on the extracted source. See [INSTALL.md](https://github.com/BD-AI-SDLC/jtr/blob/main/INSTALL.md) for manual steps and troubleshooting.

## What's new

Setup is one command instead of three, and jtr now remembers how you log in.

```bash
jtr init --ticket https://rb-tracker.bosch.com/jira/browse/PROJ-123 --auth sso
```

- **`jtr init` takes every setting directly.** It previously accepted exactly one input — a `/browse/KEY-N` ticket URL — so if you knew your base URL and project you had to fabricate a ticket URL to feed it. Now there's `--ticket`, `--base-url`, `--project`, `--auth`, `--pat`, `--browser` and `--timeout`, and each value resolves flag → parsed from the URL → existing `.env` → prompt. The URL parser also accepts a bare base URL (`https://host/jira`) rather than rejecting anything without a ticket path.
- **`--auth sso|pat` finishes the job.** init runs that login itself, so a full setup — config, bundled `/jtr` skill, and credentials — is a single command. Use `--no-auth` for the old scaffold-only behaviour.
- **Your auth method is remembered.** It's saved as `JTR_AUTH_METHOD`, so plain **`jtr auth`** re-runs whichever method this config uses — no more re-typing `sso` or `pat` every time. `jtr auth --method pat` switches the saved default. Existing setups need no migration: the method is inferred from the cookies or PAT already on disk.
- **`jtr init --force` is re-runnable.** It updates an existing `./.jtr/` in place instead of failing, and writes only the values you pass, so changing one setting doesn't blank the rest. Previously the only way to amend a project was `jtr config base-url` / `jtr config project`.
- **`--browser msedge|chrome|chromium`** records which browser SSO should drive. It's stored in the *global* `~/.jtr/.env` because it describes the machine rather than the project, and it's read from that file directly — a project-local config can never inherit the global base URL or PAT through it.
- **Safe under Claude Code and other non-TTY shells.** init never prompts when stdin isn't a terminal; it exits with the flag to pass instead of hanging on a prompt nobody can answer.
- **`jtr config show` and `jtr auth status`** now report `auth_method`, in both the table and `--json` output.

## Upgrading

Install as usual. No config, cookie, or `.env` changes are required, and existing `.env` files keep working — `JTR_AUTH_METHOD` is added on the next `jtr init` or `jtr auth sso|pat`.

Two behaviour changes worth knowing:

- **`jtr auth` with no subcommand now authenticates** instead of printing help. `jtr auth --help` still prints help.
- **`jtr init` now authenticates too** when run interactively — it asks which method to use (defaulting to `sso`) and runs it. Pass `--no-auth` to keep the previous scaffold-only behaviour. Scripts that call `jtr init` non-interactively are unaffected: without `--auth` or `--pat` there is nothing to prompt for, and init stops after scaffolding.

If init's login fails, the scaffold is deliberately kept — the config is valid either way, and `jtr auth` retries just that step.

- `install.ps1` — Windows installer
